description: This record covers the agricultural residue datasets of the 2023 Billion-Ton Study (BT23), the US Department of Energy's assessment of renewable carbon resources, hosted on the Bioenergy Knowledge Discovery Framework (KDF). They give county-level supplies of corn stover, wheat, barley and oat straw and sorghum stubble for the years 2022 to 2041 at biomass prices from $50 to $130 per dry ton, with in-field and harvested production and harvested area. The KDF is built by Oak Ridge National Laboratory with funding from the DOE Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy's Bioenergy Technologies Office. Coverage is the conterminous United States by county FIPS code and scenario. Files are CSV; the page read says access goes through the KDF contact form, and the usage policy asks users to cite each dataset's DOI, with no named licence. Caveats: values are modelled scenario projections under assumed prices and sustainability constraints, not observed harvests. For simulation it provides feedstock supply by county for capacity planning and optimisation of biorefineries, biomass power plants and their logistics networks, and for testing how droughts would cut residue supply. It is related to the Billion-Ton 2016 agricultural baseline record in this catalogue, the previous edition of the same assessment.
